claims.text: AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 is a candidate high-entropy alloy for elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance.
Controlled laser surface alloying of AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 can significantly improve its elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance relative to untreated material.
Conventionally processed AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms an uncontrolled, thin oxide layer under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
Laser surface alloying or an engineered oxidation protocol can systematically control and stabilize a dense spinel oxide layer on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The proposed protection is applicable under simultaneous oxidative corrosion and mechanical wear at approximately 700–900 °C.
A stable, dense spinel oxide scale can serve as a barrier against corrosive species.
A stable, dense spinel oxide scale can retard mechanical wear.
Controlled surface treatment promotes formation of a robust spinel oxide on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
A compact protective oxide inhibits elemental diffusion and further oxidation.
The engineered oxide barrier reduces corrosive attack on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The engineered oxide barrier reduces friction-induced wear.
Laser-treated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 will have lower wear depth than untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosive conditions.
Laser-treated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 will have a lower friction coefficient than untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
Laser-treated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 will exhibit slower oxidation kinetics than untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The non-optimized oxide on untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 leads to higher wear rates.
The non-optimized oxide on untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 leads to higher corrosion rates.
The intervention requires sufficient oxygen to form the protective spinel phase and may not work in environments that do not support oxide formation.
